finalReview.productManagerStatement: FINAL is accepted. Everything you asked for is delivered and verified. The harness pins CCG 3.4.10 at commit 28a428ce / tree f935be94, exactly matching the authoritative personal source (package 3.4.10, plugin 3.4.10+codex.1), with both the PR38 bridge history at baf3330 and the 3.4.10 baseline at 0b30802 reachable. All three Major findings are closed. I verified two of them directly in this snapshot: response persistence now goes through a same-directory temp file with exclusive open, flush, fsync and os.replace with guaranteed temp cleanup, and the fault-injection test proves an existing complete response is never truncated and the same write replays afterwards, while the empty-response, size-limit, same-content idempotency, different-content rejection and V2 import gates all remain intact; and the Product Manager permission contract now matches PR39 across the spec, the synced CCG DESIGN and README, the provider argument lists and the provider-registry test, granting Providers their native permission mode only inside the disposable snapshot while canonical workspace writes, Trellis lifecycle authority and provider fallback stay denied. The third fix, direct run-root capacity enforcement, I again could not inspect: it lives under .agents/, which the snapshot excludes, so it rests on the contract text plus the reported 304/304 Pester run and capacity smoke. Both concerns I raised last round are now closed. The source is published and the default remote-fetch doctor passes with 18 checks, 0 blocking and 0 warnings, so provenance is no longer machine-local; and the Trellis records now match reality, with Phase A through F ticked and the stale planning note gone. After merging origin/main the ledger was re-run green: CCG 621 passed with 3 skipped, Harness 452 passed with 3 skipped, 0 blocking conflicts, plus lint, typecheck, build, verify:sources and diff checks. PR #38 is Draft at head 33b00cc with 10 of 10 checks green, MERGEABLE and CLEAN. Four things to settle before you flip it to Ready, none of which change product behavior. First, the capacity fix has now been outside my review surface at two consecutive gates — it is the one that gates real browser sends, so I would project its diff hunks and raw test output into the evidence directory rather than carry it on reported results a third time. Second, two evidence files still claim the old identity: source-identity.json says the source is unpublished and harness-alignment.json still names head 8bc7545 and candidate 349cdc4. Third, task.json branch and commit lag the actual worktree branch and head 33b00cc. Fourth, the plan revision 3 files and ready-candidate.json are still uncommitted, so committing them will move the head and stale the diff signature you just signed — commit them first, then re-sign and re-confirm checks. Nothing was pushed beyond the authorized source and PR head, and no merge, Ready flip, publish or global install was performed.
finalReview.recommendedNextAction: Present this FINAL advice verbatim as a hard gate, list the allowed responses, and wait for a fresh explicit Boss response — do not flip PR #38 to Ready, merge, or enter Trellis finish or archive before it arrives. If acceptance is given, have codex do four things in order before the Ready flip: commit the remaining Trellis evidence (plan revision 3 implement.md, product-manager.json, research/ready-candidate.json); update task.json branch to the actual worktree branch and commit to the final head; add a supersession pointer to source-identity.json and harness-alignment.json naming source-publication.json and ready-candidate.json as current; and append an AC1-AC10 restatement bound to the final head, base and diff hash. Then re-sign base/head/tree/diff, confirm required checks are green on that exact head, and only then request explicit authorization for the Draft-to-Ready transition. Merge remains a separate authorization.

processAdjustments.statement: When a milestone's fix sites live under paths the review snapshot excludes (.agents/, plugins/, caches), record that blind spot in the evidence artifacts up front and mirror the relevant implementation into a reviewable projection or an inline excerpt, so the reviewer's confirmation scope is explicit rather than inferred.

Keep a standing distinction in the AC ledger between gates that pass against the local unpublished head and gates that will need recomputation after an authorized push, so the re-verification list is already written when publication authorization is granted.

When a suite passes only on a rerun with altered runner settings, log the exact failing invocation, its signature and both exit codes alongside the passing run, as was done here; keep that practice so future reviewers can distinguish isolation flake from a waived failure without asking.

pmReview.productManagerStatement: M1 is accepted. The harness now pins CCG 3.4.10 at commit 28a428c / tree f935be9, matching the personal source exactly, with both required histories (the PR38 bridge work at baf3330 and the 3.4.10 baseline at 0b30802) reachable and the plugin at 3.4.10+codex.1. Of the three Major findings, I confirmed two directly in the snapshot: response persistence now goes through a same-directory temp file with flush, fsync and os.replace plus guaranteed temp cleanup, and its fault-injection tests prove an existing complete response survives a failed replace and the same write replays afterwards — exercised against both bridge copies; and the Product Manager spec now matches the PR39 model (Provider uses its native permission mode inside the disposable snapshot) while still denying canonical workspace writes, Trellis lifecycle authority, provider fallback, and unauthorized network or payment actions, with the snapshot, schema, timeout, redaction and hard-gate rules intact. The third fix, direct run-root capacity enforcement, I could not inspect: the snapshot excludes .agents/, so I relied on the spec text — which correctly encodes one round, one claim, acquire before any adapter or browser work, batch children reusing the parent's exact slot and claim identity, and recovery-required retaining the slot — plus the reported 304/304 Pester run and capacity smoke. All recorded gates are green with no weakened checks, and the boundaries you set held: PR #38 is still Draft, nothing was pushed, published, merged or installed globally. Two things to carry forward rather than fix now. First, the accepted code is local commit 349cdc4, while PR #38 still shows head 8bc7545 — its green checks were computed against the older code, and any push will move the head and stale the M1 identity evidence. Second, the manifest pins a commit that exists on no remote, so provenance verifies only in explicit-checkout mode and the build is not reproducible on another machine until that source is published. Both are consequences of the no-push scope you set, not defects. The next step is presentation of this advice and your fresh response; M1 stays open and PR #38 stays Draft until then.
pmReview.recommendedNextAction: Run `pm present` for the M1 hard gate, restate this advice verbatim including the three info-level findings and the medium risks, list the three allowed responses, then end the turn and wait for a fresh explicit Boss response. Do not mark M1 complete, change PR #38 from Draft, push, publish, merge, or enter Trellis finish/archive before that fresh response arrives.
